subject: MediFlow throughput throttle & geo-swap request
messages:
From: Brian Liu <brian.liu@mediflow.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Cc: MediFlow SRE <sre@mediflow.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: spike in 5xx + throughput collapse - eastus2

Tessa / Redwood SRE team,

We're seeing a sudden throughput collapse and elevated 5xx rate hitting our /v1/generate integration in eastus2 starting ~08:55 PDT. Key observations:
- Overall throughput down ~60% vs baseline for the last 20m.
- p95 latency ~2.3s (baseline ~400ms).
- 5xx error rate ~8% of requests; majority are 502/504.
- Affected traffic is largely from our EU->US routing; looks like a regional AZ saturation in eastus2.

We've pulled a lean set of logs and a screenshot attached (svc_logs_0403.tar.gz, screenshot-5xx.png). Can you confirm whether this is a known capacity event or routing misconfiguration on the Redwood side? We need a short-term geo-swap to westus3 if possible — our mobile app is timing out and customers are escalating.

Please let us know ETA for mitigation and any temporary steps we should take (reduce concurrency, backoff). We're happy to accept a canary diversion if you'd prefer staged ramp.

Thanks,
Brian Liu
Head of Platform Integrations
MediFlow

Thanks Brian — I'm pulling the incident runbook now.

Plan (short term):
- Initiate a controlled geo-swap for Mediflow traffic from eastus2 -> westus3. Start with 10% canary for 10 minutes, then 100% if metrics look good.
- Enable model-quantized variant for canary to reduce memory pressure (will accept slightly different latency).
- Keep prefix cache warm and enable temporary autoprefetch for their top routes.

Dylan — can you execute the geo-swap and post the routing change commit (and command outputs) here so I can share with the customer? Use the emergency routing policy (policy id: rwp-emer-2028-04) and set canary=10.

Marissa — please prep a short exec note for our CS leadership and offer MediFlow a 10% credit for the incident window; we'll finalize after the postmortem.

I attached the runbook link: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/geo-swap

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:05:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: spike in 5xx + throughput collapse - eastus2

Tessa — executing now. Summary of actions performed:
1) Applied routing policy rwp-emer-2028-04 via control-plane:
   > rwctl routing apply --policy rwp-emer-2028-04 --target westus3 --canary 10
   Commit id: commit-9f3b2a (see attached routing-change-commit.txt)
2) Bumped canary concurrency throttle to 60 req/s for Mediflow to avoid hotshards.
3) Activated model variant: gptx-13b-q4f (quantized) for canary paths.
4) Enabled prefix cache prefetch for mediflow:/v1/generate top-50 prompts.

Initial metrics (10 minutes post canary):
- Canary p95 latency: 530ms (from 2.3s)
- Canary error rate: 0.6%
- Origin eastus2 still elevated but steady; we will continue monitoring for 20m then ramp to 100% if stable.

Attached: routing-change-commit.txt, a short snapshot of control-plane outputs and the svc logs slice.

I'll post again at the ramp decision point.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Apr 3, 2028 at 09:25 AM PDT tessa_morgan@redwood.ai wrote:
> Plan (short term): initiate controlled geo-swap...
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Brian Liu <brian.liu@mediflow.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Geo-swap completed and observed improvements

Brian — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What we did:
- Completed canary (10%) then ramped to 100% westus3 at 11:05 PDT after a successful 20m canary.
- Kept quantized variant for 40 minutes while cache warmed; switched back to standard models once pressure reduced.

Observed outcome:
- Throughput restored to baseline within ~18 minutes of ramping.
- 5xx error rate dropped from ~8% -> 0.4% (15:00 snapshot).
- p95 latency for mediflow traffic is now ~360ms.

Next steps:
- We will run a targeted postmortem and share within 48 hours. Root-cause indicators point to a combination of AZ NIC saturation and a burst of long-context requests that caused KV cache thrashing.
- Offer: 10% account credit for the incident window (will confirm with Finance).

Links: live dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/mediflow/throughput?range=6h
Postmortem doc (draft): https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/MF-2028-04-03

If you want a technical walkthrough with our runtime team, happy to schedule a 30m session today.

Thanks for flagging quickly — we appreciate the collaboration.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
